reasoning: The core problem — whether models can distinguish synthetic test/honeypot contexts from real deployment and how this scales with scenario realism — is a thoroughly studied 2025 research area. Needham et al. (arXiv 2505.23836) show frontier models classify transcripts as eval-vs-deployment with AUC>0.8; the open-weights scaling paper (arXiv 2509.13333) demonstrates power-law scaling of evaluation awareness across 15 OPEN models (0.27B-70B), directly covering the proposal's open-model and scaling claims. The proposed "direct meta-question" is exactly the documented "direct interview" method, and the realism-vs-detectability and "which surface features leak" angles are quantified by the scheming-evals work, which already identifies top leak signals (system/instruction contradictions 97%, explicit threats 89%, monitoring references 83%) and shows bimodal eval-probability dropping as realism rises. A dedicated Honeypot Protocol paper (arXiv 2604.13301) addresses honeypot detectability specifically. The only modest gap is the precise packaging (honeypot framing + graded bank + direct-ask on open models), making this a minor recombination rather than a novel contribution.

evidence.title: Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated (Needham et al.)
evidence.summary: Shows frontier LLMs classify transcripts as evaluation vs deployment with AUC>0.8, often inferring test purpose; higher discriminability in agentic contexts. Directly addresses the proposal's core detection question.

evidence.title: Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably in Open-Weights Large Language Models
evidence.summary: Studies 15 OPEN-weight models (0.27B-70B) via linear probing, finding power-law scaling of evaluation awareness with size. Covers the proposal's open-model focus and the realism/scaling dimension.

evidence.title: It's hard to make scheming evals look realistic for LLMs
evidence.summary: Uses LLM-judge probability grading of scenario realism, identifies which surface features leak that a scenario is a test (system/instruction contradictions 97%, explicit threats 89%, monitoring references 83%), and shows rewriting toward realism only modestly reduces eval-probability — directly covering the 'which features make a honeypot leak' question.

evidence.title: Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness of Language Models
evidence.summary: Linear probes for test-vs-deployment that generalize across real-world testing and deployment prompts, demonstrating models internally represent the synthetic/real distinction; also explores steering.

evidence.title: Honeypot Protocol (AI Control Hackathon 2026)
evidence.summary: Directly addresses the honeypot detectability problem for AI control, proposing generator-discriminator and synthetic-document approaches to make honeypot contexts indistinguishable from real deployment.

evidence.title: Probe-Rewrite-Evaluate: A Workflow for Reliable Benchmarks and Quantifying Evaluation Awareness
evidence.summary: Training-free pipeline assigning continuous realism scores to prompts and measuring behavior shifts from test-like to deploy-like contexts; quantifies detectability as a function of realism.
